pages.text: $(thing)City Ages$() no longer grow as one dead square repeated to the horizon. They gather around many hearts: old civic crowns, brick wards, garden quarters, industrial scars, and pale marina fronts, all crowding and leaning into one another.

Where two city-hearts draw near, roads fatten into avenues, and beyond them the long raised ways begin their crawl from district to district. Some routes dive below the stone as rail cuts and station halls. Others bridge water, ravine, or ruin rather than yield.

Because of this, a City Age should feel less like a board laid flat and more like a realm lived in badly for centuries. Expect tower clusters, apartment belts, trimmed parks, sudden courtyards, and quieter suburbs between the louder wounds.

$(thing)Biosphere Ages$() are black emptiness strung with glassy gardens. Each sphere may hold a true biome, even one born from distant mods, and with it may come the creatures, air, and habits of that place.
Neither city nor biosphere appears by accident very often. If one blooms from an unwritten chance, assume the Age is proud, strange, and not especially interested in your continued health.
